title: Perf gates iterate the page registry: the seventh page has no 10x line

body:
## Summary
The perf gate is a hand-list. Seven pages are registered (app/pages.ts:11), six have 10x DOM and RPC lines (budgets/perf.json:4-26), and the three perf suites each re-list those six by hand. Session review shipped as the seventh page with bundle lines (the bundle gate derives routes and refuses an unbudgeted one) and with no 10x line at all, and nothing went red. Make the measured page set a typed table keyed by PageId, have every perf suite iterate it, and add a two-way coverage check, then give review its lines.

## Description
quality-gates / item-liveness and metric-gates / counted-set-snapshot: a gate whose population is a hand-list stops covering new items silently; the gate must be keyed by the identity of what it governs and refuse an item with no line, the way check-bundle.mjs:91-92 already does for routes. Here the identity is PageId.

- `src/perf/pages.tsx` (new): `PERF_PAGES = {...} satisfies Record<PageId, PerfPage>`, where a PerfPage is `{ l1: Probe; l2?: Record<string, Probe> } | { exempt: string }` and a Probe is `{ ui, script, hash, ready? }`. The six existing probes move here verbatim from dom.test.tsx (same hashes, same ready predicates), so their measured counts do not change.
- dom.test.tsx, rpc.test.tsx and timings.test.tsx become loops over PERF_PAGES (it.each), keeping each line's name (`<page>.l1`, `<page>.l2.<list>`).
- `src/perf/coverage.test.ts` (new): PERF_PAGES keys equal PAGE_IDS; every measured name has a dom line and every l1 an rpc line; every perf.json dom/rpc key is measured by some entry; an exemption has a non-empty reason.
- fixture.ts gains `reviewScript()` over `sessionRows(SCALE.streams)` and `bigSession({ events: SCALE.transcriptLines, ... })`; perf.json gains `review.l1`, `review.l2.timeline` (dom) and `review.l1` (rpc) at measured + ~8%, the existing margin rule (perf.json:2).

The compile-time Record<PageId,...> catches a new page at typecheck; the runtime test catches orphan and missing budget lines, which the type cannot.

## Flow
- Builder writes coverage.test.ts first: it fails (no PERF_PAGES, no review lines).
- Move the six probes into pages.tsx; convert the three suites to iterate; run `test -- src/perf`: the six existing lines still pass at their current counts.
- Add reviewScript and the review probes; measure; write the review lines with their `why`.
- coverage.test.ts passes; typecheck proves the Record is exhaustive.

## Expected impact
The 10x gate covers every page the console ships, and the next page cannot land without declaring its DOM and RPC lines (or a written exemption). The per-page wiring that is today spelled three times (dom, rpc, timings) is spelled once. Review, whose layer 2 holds 100k-line sessions and six tabs, gets its first scale measurement.

## Evaluation
Claim: the perf gates cover exactly the registered page set, both ways, and review is held to a 10x line.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no PERF_PAGES; review has no dom/rpc line; nothing compares perf.json keys to pages)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: architecture (test-suite structure only; no production code, no contract)
evidence: pages.ts:11 `export const PAGES = { onair, characters, brain, segments, simulator, review, reconcile } satisfies PageRegistry;` | `grep -rn review apps/console/src/perf | wc -l` -> 0 | perf.json dom keys: onair.l1, characters.l1, brain.l1, segments.l1, simulator.l1, reconcile.l1, onair.l2.rundown, characters.l2.all, brain.l2.runs, brain.l2.transcript, segments.l2.tables, simulator.l2.runs, reconcile.l2.report (no review) | rpc keys: onair.l1, characters.l1, brain.l1, segments.l1, simulator.l1, reconcile.l1 | check-bundle.mjs:91-92 `for (const name of Object.keys(BUDGETS.routes)) { if (!(name in measured)) failures.push(`${name}: budgeted but no such route was built`); }` | bundle.json:56 `"review.l1": {`, :60 `"review.l2": {`

critic.reason: Sound gate redesign, but one acceptance case contradicts the page's actual first-paint calls.

revision: Rewrite case 6: review layer 1 first paint at 10x -> the RPC tally is exactly {review.sessions: 1, review.feedback.list: 1} (what Layer1.tsx:30-31 calls today), and any other method (e.g. review.session) fails as unlisted.

title: Owner exceptions live as hand-edits a recapture erases: make them an overlay
acceptance: contract {characters:{halftoneA:{opacity:'0.55'}}} + exception {target:'texture', key:'characters.halftoneA', prop:'opacity', winner:'0.55', port:'0', why, decided, ref} -> applyExceptions returns a contract holding '0' there and problems []
same exception but the contract (a fresh capture) holds winner '0.6' -> problem 'characters.halftoneA.opacity: the winner moved from 0.55 to 0.6 under an owner exception; re-decide it', run exits 1
exception keyed characters.halftoneC (no such layer) -> problem 'matches nothing in contract.texture.json', run exits 1 (never silently dropped)
exception with an empty why or no decided date -> rejected as unparseable, run exits 1
two exceptions on characters.grain.opacity -> problem 'duplicate exception', run exits 1

committed contract.texture.json + committed exceptions.json, offline (no Playwright, no contest data) -> every exception's winner value equals the committed contract value and the six characters/segments opacities in the contract are the winner's (0.55 / 0.35 / 0.4), not '0'
`node fidelity/run.mjs` summary with exceptions honoured -> prints 'N owner exception(s) applied' with each key, so a green run names what it waived
premise: apps/console/fidelity/roles.json:40 - the texture exception is recorded as prose: 'contract.texture.json holds "0" for characters and segments where the winner had 0.4; a fresh `texture.py capture` writes the winner's 0.4 back, so re-apply the exception after one'

apps/console/fidelity/contract.texture.json:4,12,20,56,64,72 - six captured winner values hand-edited to "0" (halftoneA, halftoneB, grain on characters and segments); git show 0d7a5a2 shows 0.55->0 and 0.35->0 edited directly into the captured file
apps/console/fidelity/texture.py:94-95 - capture mode overwrites the whole contract file with fresh measurements, so the hand-edits are lost on every recapture

apps/console/fidelity/texture.py:103-122 - check compares port against the contract verbatim; it has no notion of a sanctioned difference, so after a recapture the gate demands the port re-add grain and halftone under body text, the opposite of the owner's decision (packages/tokens/REJECTED.md:18-22)
apps/console/fidelity/run.mjs:84,91 - per-page contracts are passed straight to style-contract.py (an external skill tool) with no seam where a sanctioned difference could be applied
apps/console/fidelity/run.mjs:98-100 - the texture contract is passed as a path to texture.py, so a merged copy written to the run's tmp dir (run.mjs:74) needs no change to either Python tool
apps/console/fidelity/run.mjs:110 - the summary prints only each tool's last line; nothing says which differences were owner-approved
rollback: Revert the series: contract.texture.json returns to its hand-edited '0' values, roles.json:40 regains its prose instruction, exceptions.json/.mjs/.test.mjs go, and run.mjs passes contract files directly again. No product code or contract package is touched.
test_command: node --test apps/console/fidelity/exceptions.test.mjs && pnpm -C apps/console typecheck && FIDELITY_REQUIRED=1 pnpm -C apps/console fidelity (local, with SHADOWRUNR_CONTEST_DATA set)
runner_up: Budget raises as a structured ledger: replace bundle.json's ~4 KB prose $comment (and perf.json's free-text why) with {line, from, to, measured, date, why} entries and a ratchet check that flags slack (e.g. simulator.l1 dom line 84 over a measured 55)
body:
## Summary
The fidelity gate's oracle is a captured copy of the winning prototype, and the owner has twice decided the port should differ from it (no grain, then no halftone, on the light posters). Both decisions were applied by hand-editing six captured numbers to "0", with a prose note telling whoever recaptures to re-apply them. A recapture therefore erases the owner's decision and turns the gate against it. Record exceptions as a named overlay applied at check time, restore the captured file to what was captured, and make every exception loud when it no longer matches.

## Description
quality-gates / waiver-names-its-finding (one waiver, one finding; a waiver that names nothing is reported, not honoured or dropped) and oracle-frozen-during-repair (the oracle must not be edited to make the port pass). Each exception names its target contract, key, property, the winner value it overrides, the port value, why, the decision date and a ref (packages/tokens/REJECTED.md).

- `fidelity/exceptions.json` (new): the six current exceptions, moved out of contract.texture.json.
- `fidelity/exceptions.mjs` (new): `parseExceptions(json)` and `applyExceptions(contract, exceptions, target) -> { contract, applied, problems }`. Problems: unparseable (missing why/decided/port), unmatched key or prop, winner moved, duplicate.
- `run.mjs`: in check mode, write a merged copy of each contract (page contracts and texture) into its tmp dir (run.mjs:74) and hand that path to style-contract.py / texture.py, so neither Python tool changes; any problem fails the run; the summary lists the applied exceptions. In capture mode, after writing, re-run applyExceptions against the fresh capture and report any winner that moved.
- `contract.texture.json`: the six values go back to the winner's captured 0.55 / 0.35 / 0.4.
- `roles.json:40`: the 're-apply after recapture' instruction is replaced by a pointer to exceptions.json.
- `package.json`: a `fidelity:exceptions` script running the offline check, the one part of the fidelity gate that needs neither Playwright nor the contest data.

## Flow
- Write exceptions.test.mjs first (cases 1-6): all fail, the module does not exist.
- Build exceptions.mjs; cases 1-5 pass.
- Move the six values into exceptions.json and restore the contract; case 6 passes.
- Wire run.mjs; run the local fidelity gate with FIDELITY_REQUIRED=1: still 0 deviations, now with '6 owner exception(s) applied'.

## Expected impact
A recapture can no longer silently reverse an owner design decision or make the gate demand one be undone; a winner change under an exception surfaces as 're-decide this', not as a deviation someone fixes by re-adding grain. The captured contract means 'what the winner is' again, and the exceptions become a countable, dated list instead of prose in a $comment.

## Evaluation
Claim: owner exceptions survive a recapture and every exception is either applied, or reported with a reason.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no exception model; the contract holds hand-edited values; a recapture writes the winner's values back)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: architecture (gate tooling only; it tightens the oracle, loosens nothing)
evidence: roles.json:40 `... a fresh `texture.py capture` writes the winner's 0.4 back, so re-apply the exception after one. The same exception (UI-3, 2026-10-20) takes the halftone dots off the open characters and segments posters ... halftoneA and halftoneB hold \"0\" there too.` | git show 0d7a5a2 -- apps/console/fidelity/contract.texture.json: `-      "opacity": "0.55",` `+      "opacity": "0",` (x2 per page, characters and segments) | texture.py:94-95 `if a.mode == "capture": Path(a.contract).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", ...)` | grep -n '"opacity"' contract.texture.json -> 4:"0", 12:"0", 20:"0", 56:"0", 64:"0", 72:"0" against 0.55/0.35/0.4 on onair, reconcile, brain, simulator

critic.reason: True premise and crisp offline cases. Modest ambition, but it clears the floors.
